note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English; the original treats Anoplotermes sedatus as a new synonym of this species, and the synonymy list is not translated. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The characters distinguishing it from A. aneristus, A. apocnetus, A. hilarus and A. mansuetus are given under those species. Compared with the type species of the genus, A. prosenus, the present species is smaller, with proportionally smaller compound eyes and ocelli, a shorter mandibular apical tooth and different proportions of the marginal teeth of the right mandible; the fontanelle of A. prosenus is circular and shallow. The worker of A. prosenus also has a longer apical tooth, a more inflated postclypeus and a slightly thicker fore tibia. The worker abdomen of the present species is dehiscent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule yellowish white; pilosity sparse, yellow. Postclypeus weakly to moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.22–0.29, Pcl/Rj 1.65–2.38. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.40–0.49, Ra/Ri 0.62–0.71; in surface view the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence, La/Li·Lm 7.47–9.56; the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are roughly aligned, the anterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth equal, Ra/Ri·Rm 8.86–13.92. Fore tibia very slender, Ti/Tw 5.77–7.08; third apical spur distinct. The midgut–hindgut overlap is oblique and lies to the right of the Malpighian tubule knot; in the unopened abdomen the enteric valve seat is slightly dorsal, on the right side, distinctly bilobed, and joined to the second hindgut pouch by a short neck; the valve membrane bears minute spines outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule dark brown, not darker above the ocelli; fontanelle of moderate size but less than half the ocellus, elliptical, flat, pale brown; central spot very small, almost obsolete, broadly elliptical, brown; postclypeus brown, labrum yellow; frontal groove small, flat, semicircular, brown; antennae brown. Pronotum dark brown, meso- and metanotum brown, transverse sutures present; femora yellowish brown, tibiae paler, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites dark brown, dorsal spiracles pale yellowish brown, ventral spiracles similar, the lateral parts of the sternites pale brown and the median part paler, cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule broadly arcuate, slightly undulate; compound eyes and ocelli both large, their distance at most one third of the minimum diameter of the ocellus; postclypeus weakly inflated, Pcl/W 0.19–0.23, posterior margin arcuate or undulate, not evenly rounded, median suture present but not always complete. Mandibular apical tooth short, La/Li 0.46–0.60, Ra/Ri 0.58–0.78; in surface view the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible just clears the molar prominence, La/L1·Lm 4.70–8.11; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are roughly aligned, and the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth is almost twice as long as that of the second. Meso- and metanotum moderately broad at the constriction, M/W 0.29–0.32. Cephalic pilosity dense and even, forming a layer, with longer outstanding setae.
